analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: USTs are supported, extending the prior day's risk-off bull-steepening, but the rally is modest relative to equity weakness. 10Y UST yields remain above 5.10% and DXY is just below 103.50.

The S&P fell 1.9%, Nasdaq 2.5% and semis 5.3% the prior day, with the sell-off extending into Asia after the US tightened restrictions on access to advanced AI chips. Mizuho sees the equity/rates beta as the more interesting part of the story.
USTs are responding to the equity sell-off but not aggressively, consistent with a market still reluctant to fade the hawkish Fed repricing.

Today's Fed speak and retail sales are the key US macro catalysts. Consensus expects a sharp slowdown from September and Mizuho sees some downside risk. A soft print plus another leg lower in equities would give the belly more room to rally.
Brent fell more than 3% on Monday to below $92 as a potential Q4 supply surplus narrative outweighed Iran/Hormuz risks. Lower oil should support duration at the margin.
JD Vance pushed back against the idea of a prolonged US war. Tanker incidents continue and reports of Iranian contingency plans targeting US officials keep geopolitical tail risks alive.

EGBs are better bid and EUR/USD is around 1.10 after bouncing off Monday's lows. About 65bp of ECB tightening is priced in the curve. Mizuho will watch whether Makhlouf and Lane validate it, though Brent below $92 should counterweight the hawkish repricing if sustained.

Knot is reportedly expected to drop out of the ECB president race this week, boosting De Cos's chances. Mizuho reads this as slightly dovish at the margin, but notes De Cos is a consensus-builder and the other two Executive Board appointments matter just as much for rates.
UK labour data gave a mixed read on slack. September private earnings ex-bonus were 3.1% 3M/YoY, as expected. Unemployment fell to 4.6% vs 4.7% expected. October payrolls fell 34k vs +10k consensus.

Mizuho says the UK payroll miss gives front-end SONIA room to rally and makes the December BoE meeting a closer call, but sticky wages and falling unemployment mean December is not written off. Monthly payrolls are volatile and often revised.
Tomorrow's UK inflation print, especially services inflation, is the next test of whether the slack/wage dynamic is reducing domestic inflation persistence.
In Japan, JGB moves were contained and the curve twist-steepened ahead of tomorrow's 20Y JGB auction. USD/JPY fell below 159.40.
